key_insight: States already prepared for dynamical quantum response simulations can also reveal how information propagates, becomes locally accessible, and supports quantum communication and entanglement.
engineering_relevance: Reusing response-simulation protocols could broaden quantum simulator diagnostics without designing a separate state-preparation scheme for each information task.
method: Study local-pulse Green-function protocols in finite XX and XXX spin chains.
Encode a classical bit with opposite source rotations and track its propagation and local readout.
Use reduced states to assess source-angle estimation, Bell-state recovery, communication rates, and entanglement.
evidence_signal: In the studied chains, fermionic covariance data exactly reconstruct the signed XX response, yet simple spin measurements recover a larger fraction of locally available information in XXX; this readout ordering persists for source-angle estimation.
watch_item: The case study concerns finite spin chains; scalability and robustness to experimental noise are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Dynamical quantum simulations as laboratories for quantum information
